metadata.description: Database of known breaking changes and compatibility issues for GeoServer infrastructure components

breakingChanges.title: REST API Layer Groups Schema Change
breakingChanges.description: REST API endpoints for layer groups changed structure and response format
breakingChanges.impact: Custom scripts using layer group REST API will break. GET /rest/layergroups returns different JSON structure.
breakingChanges.remediation: Update REST API calls to use new layerGroup schema format. See: https://docs.geoserver.org/stable/en/user/rest/api/layergroups.html

breakingChanges.title: Default Workspace Handling Changed
breakingChanges.description: Default workspace behavior for services without explicit workspace prefix has changed
breakingChanges.impact: Services without workspace prefix may resolve to different workspaces than before. WMS/WFS requests without workspace may behave differently.
breakingChanges.remediation: Review and explicitly set default workspace in global.xml. Update client applications to always specify workspace in requests.

breakingChanges.title: Legacy GeoJSON Output Format Deprecated
breakingChanges.description: Old GeoJSON output format (application/json) deprecated in favor of standard application/geo+json
breakingChanges.impact: Clients using application/json MIME type will receive deprecation warnings
breakingChanges.remediation: Update client applications to request application/geo+json instead of application/json

breakingChanges.title: Security Subsystem Refactored
breakingChanges.description: Complete refactoring of security subsystem with new authentication/authorization API
breakingChanges.impact: Custom authentication providers and security filters will not load. Extensions using old security API will fail.
breakingChanges.remediation: Migrate custom auth filters to new security API. Consult migration guide: https://docs.geoserver.org/latest/en/developer/programming-guide/security/index.html
breakingChanges.detectionMethod: Check for custom .jar files in WEB-INF/lib matching pattern: *auth*.jar, *security*.jar

breakingChanges.title: Minimum Java Version Raised to 11
breakingChanges.description: Java 8 no longer supported. GeoServer requires Java 11 or later.
breakingChanges.impact: Java 8 installations will fail to start with ClassNotFoundException or UnsupportedClassVersionError
breakingChanges.remediation: Upgrade Java to version 11, 17, or 21 before upgrading GeoServer. Recommended: Use Java 17 LTS.

breakingChanges.title: Style Configuration Format Updated
breakingChanges.description: Style configuration XML schema updated to support CSS 3 features and new rendering hints
breakingChanges.impact: Some legacy SLD styles may not validate. Complex SLD with vendor options may need review.
breakingChanges.remediation: Run style validation tool on all SLD files. Update styles using deprecated vendor options. Test rendering output.
breakingChanges.detectionMethod: Scan data_directory/styles for .sld files, check for deprecated vendor options

breakingChanges.title: WPS Process API Changes
breakingChanges.description: WPS process execution API updated with new asynchronous execution model
breakingChanges.impact: Custom WPS processes need migration. Synchronous-only processes may behave differently.
breakingChanges.remediation: Update custom WPS processes to support async execution. Review WPS client timeout settings.
breakingChanges.detectionMethod: Check for WPS extension installation and custom process JARs

breakingChanges.title: GeoWebCache Default Settings Changed
breakingChanges.description: Default tile cache expiration and disk quota settings changed
breakingChanges.impact: Existing tile caches may need reconfiguration. Disk usage patterns may change.
breakingChanges.remediation: Review GeoWebCache configuration. Adjust disk quotas and expiration policies as needed.

breakingChanges.title: PostgreSQL Minimum Version Raised
breakingChanges.description: Minimum PostgreSQL version raised to 12.0 for PostGIS stores
breakingChanges.impact: PostgreSQL 11 and earlier versions no longer supported
breakingChanges.remediation: Upgrade PostgreSQL to version 12 or later before upgrading GeoServer

breakingChanges.title: Servlet 4.0 API Changes
breakingChanges.description: Upgraded to Servlet 4.0 specification with HTTP/2 support
breakingChanges.impact: Applications using Servlet 3.1 deprecated features may fail. HTTP/2 push APIs different.
breakingChanges.remediation: Update web applications to Servlet 4.0 specification. Remove deprecated API usage.

breakingChanges.title: Default TLS Protocol Changes
breakingChanges.description: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 disabled by default. TLS 1.2+ required.
breakingChanges.impact: Clients using TLS 1.0/1.1 will fail to connect to HTTPS connectors
breakingChanges.remediation: Update SSL/TLS configuration to require TLS 1.2 minimum. Update client applications.

breakingChanges.title: Java 11 Minimum Requirement
breakingChanges.description: Tomcat 10 requires Java 11 or later. Java 8 no longer supported.
breakingChanges.impact: Java 8 installations will fail to start
breakingChanges.remediation: Upgrade to Java 11 or later before upgrading Tomcat

breakingChanges.title: Jakarta EE Namespace Migration
breakingChanges.description: Complete migration from javax.* to jakarta.* package namespace
breakingChanges.impact: ALL applications using javax.servlet.*, javax.websocket.*, javax.el.* will NOT work. Requires application recompilation.
breakingChanges.remediation: Option 1: Stay on Tomcat 9.x (recommended for GeoServer). Option 2: Migrate applications to Jakarta EE 9+ (requires source code changes and recompilation).
breakingChanges.notes: GeoServer does NOT support Tomcat 10+ as of GeoServer 2.25. Use Tomcat 9.0.x branch.

compatibility.geoserver: NOT COMPATIBLE - GeoServer requires Tomcat 9.x or earlier

breakingChanges.title: Default Connector Settings Changed
breakingChanges.description: Default maxThreads, maxConnections, and other connector parameters adjusted
breakingChanges.impact: Performance characteristics may differ from Tomcat 10.0.x
breakingChanges.remediation: Review and explicitly configure connector settings in server.xml

breakingChanges.title: Java 17 Minimum Requirement
breakingChanges.description: Tomcat 11 requires Java 17 or later
breakingChanges.impact: Java 11 installations will fail to start
breakingChanges.remediation: Upgrade to Java 17 or 21 before upgrading Tomcat

breakingChanges.title: Java EE Modules Removed
breakingChanges.description: Java EE and CORBA modules removed from JDK (JAXB, JAX-WS, etc.)
breakingChanges.impact: Applications using JAXB, JAX-WS, or other Java EE APIs will fail with ClassNotFoundException
breakingChanges.remediation: Add required libraries as dependencies. For JAXB add: jakarta.xml.bind:jakarta.xml.bind-api:3.0.1

breakingChanges.title: Nashorn JavaScript Engine Deprecated
breakingChanges.description: Nashorn JavaScript engine deprecated (removed in Java 15)
breakingChanges.impact: Scripts using Nashorn will receive deprecation warnings
breakingChanges.remediation: Migrate to GraalVM JavaScript or alternative scripting engine

breakingChanges.title: Security Manager Deprecated for Removal
breakingChanges.description: Security Manager deprecated and will be removed in future release
breakingChanges.impact: Applications relying on Security Manager will need migration path
breakingChanges.remediation: Plan migration away from Security Manager. Use OS-level security instead.

breakingChanges.title: Stronger Encapsulation of JDK Internals
breakingChanges.description: Illegal reflective access to internal APIs blocked by default
breakingChanges.impact: Libraries using reflection to access internal JDK classes may fail
breakingChanges.remediation: Update libraries to use public APIs. Add --add-opens JVM flags as temporary workaround.

breakingChanges.title: Thread.stop() Permanently Deprecated
breakingChanges.description: Thread.stop() throws UnsupportedOperationException
breakingChanges.impact: Code calling Thread.stop() will fail at runtime
breakingChanges.remediation: Use cooperative thread interruption instead of Thread.stop()
